title: Your First Visual Novel Game
description: Build an interactive visual novel with character portraits, typewriter dialogue, variable interpolation, and branching player choices.

blocks.content: In this tutorial, you will build a playable visual novel scene in about **20 minutes**. Your scene will display a background illustration, switch character emotion portraits automatically, stream dialogue with a typewriter effect, and present branching choice buttons.

items.title: Typewriter Dialogue
items.desc: Stream dialogue lines character by character with click or key-press fast-forwarding.

items.title: Emotion Portraits
items.desc: Swap character sprites and speaker name colors automatically for each line.

items.title: Branching Choices
items.desc: Present interactive choice buttons that route the story to different dialogue IDs.

items.title: Variable Tokens
items.desc: Insert dynamic player names and stats directly inside dialogue strings.

blocks.content: Complete [Quick Start](getting_started/quick_start) first to learn how projects, entities, and scripts work. Import a background image and two or more character portrait images (such as **neutral** and **happy** expressions) into the **Assets** dock.

rows: Draws the background artwork, character portrait, dialogue box panel, and choice buttons.
Renders the speaker name, dialogue body text, and choice button captions.
Reads the character and dialogue maps, updates portraits, and streams typewriter text.
Shows branching choice buttons when a dialogue entry includes player options.

blocks.content: First, create the visual novel layout on a UI layer in the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy) using the exact entity IDs expected by [Dialogue Runner](node_library/helper_tool#node-vnDialogueRunner) and [Choice Presenter](node_library/helper_tool#node-vnChoicePresenter).

items: In the **Scene Hierarchy**, create a background entity on your world layer and attach [Image Renderer](components/renderers/sprite_renderer) with your scene background texture.
Create a character portrait entity named **spriteCharacter**, attach **Image Renderer**, and position it near the center of the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport).

On your **UI** layer, create a dialogue panel at the bottom of the screen using [Shape Renderer](components/renderers/shape_renderer), and add a child [Text Renderer](components/renderers/text_renderer) entity named **dialogText**.
Above the left corner of the dialogue panel, create a speaker badge shape named **nameBox** and a child **Text Renderer** entity named **characterName**.

In the center of the screen, create three button entities named **btnChoice1**, **btnChoice2**, and **btnChoice3**, each with a child **Text Renderer** named **btnChoice1Text**, **btnChoice2Text**, and **btnChoice3Text**.
In the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), uncheck **Visible** on **btnChoice1**, **btnChoice2**, and **btnChoice3** so the choice buttons stay hidden until a branching point occurs.

blocks.content: Next, store your cast metadata in a **charMap** object and your story script in a **dialogMap** object using [Variables & Collections](visual_scripting/variables_and_collections) or a [Custom Node](visual_scripting/custom_node_and_code).

blocks.message: Set **speaker** to **narrator** (or leave it empty) on any dialogue entry to automatically hide **nameBox**, **characterName**, and **spriteCharacter** during narration lines.

blocks.content: Connect [Dialogue Runner](node_library/helper_tool#node-vnDialogueRunner) and [Choice Presenter](node_library/helper_tool#node-vnChoicePresenter) in a [Script Controller](components/script_controller) graph so the conversation advances and branches automatically.

items: Create a **DialogueManager** entity, attach **Script Controller**, and open its graph in the [Graph & Node Concepts](visual_scripting/graph_concepts) editor.
Add [On Scene Start](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventSceneStart) and connect its execution output to **Dialogue Runner**.
Connect your character map to **charMap**, your dialogue map to **dialogMap**, and set **dialogId** to **intro_1** (or leave **dialogId** empty to start from the first key automatically).
Wire the **onNext** execution output of **Dialogue Runner** back into the **execIn** input of **Dialogue Runner**, and wire **nextDialogId** into **dialogId** so clicking advances to the next line.
Wire the **onChoice** execution output and the **choices** list output of **Dialogue Runner** into **Choice Presenter**.
Connect the **execOut** output and **nextDialogId** output of **Choice Presenter** back into **Dialogue Runner** so clicking a choice button jumps to the selected story branch.

blocks.content: Run the visual novel in the viewport and test both story branches.

items: Click **Play** in the top bar. **Alya**'s portrait appears and the first line streams across **dialogText**.
Click the screen (or press **Space**, **Enter**, or **Z**) while text is typing to reveal the full line immediately.
When the two choice buttons (**btnChoice1** and **btnChoice2**) appear, click either option to verify that the buttons hide and **Dialogue Runner** jumps to the chosen branch.
Click **Stop** in the top bar and press **Ctrl + S** to save your project.

blocks.message: You can insert variable tokens such as **{playerName}** inside any dialogue **text** or choice **text** field, and **Dialogue Runner** will replace them with your local or global variable values at runtime.

blocks.content: Download the completed Visual Novel **.lupisproject** sample archive to inspect the UI hierarchy, dialogue maps, and branching node graph directly in the editor.

rows: Complete dialogue UI layout, multi-emotion character portraits, typewriter effect, variable tokens, and branching choices.

items: Click the download link in the table above to save the **.lupisproject** archive to your computer.
Open the **My Projects** dashboard in Lupis Engine (see [Project & Export](getting_started/project_and_export#manage-projects)).
Drag and drop the downloaded **.lupisproject** file onto the dashboard, or click **Load Project** and select the file.
Click the imported project card to open the editor, then click **Play** in the top bar to play through the visual novel.
